## Verdict: NOISY

Same-model reruns differ by a sizeable fraction of the inter-compiler distance: inter-compiler variance carries information, but a delta smaller than the noise floor should not be read as an effect.

*Structural distance = mean of normalized LOC delta, AST-node delta and import-set Jaccard distance -- the one function shared by lang-compare, bench and bench-r2. n=2 per model is the minimum that yields a floor at all; it is a floor, not a distribution. The ratio is printed to 2 decimals on purpose: the AST-node count differs between Python versions (ast.walk on 3.8 vs 3.13), so a ratio can move by up to ~0.26 across interpreters without any code or model changing -- classes are stable across 3.8/3.13 on this bench, ratios are not point-precise, and an entry within ~0.25 of a threshold should be read as borderline.*
